acceptance: Durations file exists and is refreshed by nightly (after dlv2-22)
Budget check fails CI when a T1 test exceeds 0.5 s without an exemption
Quarantine marker enforced: missing owner/expiry/issue or past expiry fails collection; quarantined tests run in T3
tests/unit/test_marker_strategy.py rewritten to assert the tier rules instead of workflow lane coverage
context: Measured 2026-09-28: unit tier 239 s on 8 local workers; slow+resource_heavy (98 tests) 78 s.
description:
Markers do not match measured cost (e.g. tests/unit/platforms/pyspark/test_pyspark_sql_smoke.py is `medium`; ~124 tests >=1 s take ~47% of measured unit time). Implement:
1. A committed durations file (per-test p95 seconds) regenerated by T3 nightly; T1 shard balancing reads it (pytest-xdist --dist worksteal plus duration-balanced shards).
2. Tier assignment by duration: tests over 0.5 s leave T1 for T2 unless they carry a documented exemption with an expiry date; a check fails T1 on a new unexempted slow test.
3. `@pytest.mark.quarantine(owner=..., expiry=..., issue=...)`: skipped in T1/T2, still run in T3; an expired quarantine fails collection.
